**International Copper Study Group Statistical Committee Thirty-Fourth Regular Meeting 6**<sup>**th**</sup> **October 2009, 4.00pm-6.00pm Lisbon, Portugal** 

**ICSG/STAT34/4** 

## **Statistical Committee Report on progress in 2009/2010 Statistical Committee Work Program (Agenda Item 7)** 

The Statistical Committee provides a forum between member governments, industry and third parties connected to the copper industry to exchange information on copper and to discuss issues related to copper statistics. 

The three main objectives of ICSG statistical work are to improve statistics on copper, to increase market transparency and to undertake studies on issues related to copper that are of interest to member governments and industry.  In order to fulfill this, the Committee produces a series of publications on copper statistics, forecast and undertakes a range of activities and projects specified in its work program. 

Further to the detailed work program and projects presented during the Group’s last session in April 2009, the following update describes the progress that has so far been made in what concerns the regular statistical work and the statistical approved projects. A summary table of the Statistical Regular Work Program and Projects is also presented at the end of this document. 

## **<u>Regular Activities</u>** 

<u>Data collection/Data Gaps/Data Research (Item S1)</u> 

Data is the backbone of all ICSG statistical work and outputs. Besides receiving data from some of its members, the secretariat, with the aim of improving the world coverage, dedicates a significant part of its working time to collect data from other sources such as metals associations, company direct contacts and quarterly reports, national statistical offices and specialized press.  After being checked for possible inconsistencies, all the data collected is inserted in the ICSG statistical database on a daily basis.  The secretariat continuously undertakes research/analysis work on data inconsistencies or gaps and looks for new reliable data sources.  Special attention is being given this year to secondary smelter and refined production data as a complement to the scrap project.  Research on semis production data is also being pursued to improve input to the recycling survey assessment. Research for reliable data sources for some countries such as Vietnam, Georgia, Myanmar, Uzbekistan, etc is also undertaken.  The efforts of the secretariat to continue providing the best possible reliable data will continue as one of the main aims of the Statistical Committee. 

<u>Monthly Copper Bulletin (Item S2)</u> ICSG produces a Copper Bulletin every month as a result of its continued work on improving and updating its statistics, and with the aim of keeping member countries, industry and subscribers regularly informed.  In order to provide a better service to member countries and subscribers, the secretariat started this year to distribute, in addition to the PDF version of th

e Bulletin, Excel tables to allow readers to easily use ICSG data for analytical purposes.  The acceptance of ICSG Bulletin as a transparent and reliable source of copper data is increasing and allowing for an easier use of the Bulletin data through Excel tables was welcomed by readers.  Since the last meeting, 5 Bulletins were prepared and published. The Bulletin represented as well an important source of revenue for ICSG through its sales. Since the April 2009 meeting 5 Bulletins were published.  Additional charts are planned to be included this year in the Bulletin. 

1 

<u>Press Releases (Item S3)</u> The secretariat produces and distributes a press release to the public, summarizing market conditions and balance situation, with the publication of each monthly Copper Bulletin, each Directory of Copper Mines and Plants (bi-annual), each Forecast (bi-annual) and each Statistical Yearbook.  This service has helped to expand the coverage of the Group’s work and as such has increased the general awareness of its activities. The secretariat works closely with the Statistical Committee Chairman on the preparation of the press releases. Since the April 2009 meeting five press releases were issued with the publication of the Bulletins, one with the release of the June 2009 Directory of Mines and Plants and one with the publication of the 2009 Statistical Yearbook. 

– <u>Directory of Copper Mines & Plants Capacities (Item S4) The ICSG publishes an up-to-date</u> version of this Directory twice yearly. The Directory highlights current production capacity and provides a five year outlook of forecasted capacity for over 1,000 existing and planned copper mines, plants and refineries on a country by country basis, including separate tables for SX-EW plants.  Salient details for each operation are included and operations are categorized by Operating & Developing and Exploration & Feasibility stages.  The secretariat published a Directory in June 2009 and the next edition is scheduled for publication in December 2009.  The Directory represents a source of revenue for ICSG through it sales. 

<u>World Copper Forecast (Item S5)</u> Twice per year ICSG prepares forecasts for the copper market, presenting a two year outlook. For this purpose, the Study Group seeks the important collaboration of its members by asking them to complete a Forecast survey showing the expected evolution for the copper industry in their countries. The results of the survey are complemented with additional data gathered from other sources, such as industry/company data and discussions with industry experts. Estimates are set for the countries where no specific data is received/available. A slide presentation is also prepared and presented at the Statistical Committee meetings followed by a forum discussion. The last forecast was presented at the April 2009 meeting and the next one is currently being prepared and will be presented at the October 2009 meeting. 

<u>Trade Flow Matrixes (I

tem S6)</u> ICSG prepares once a year trade matrixes that indicate the flows of copper concentrates, blister, refined copper and copper scrap, by origin and destination.  Trade flows are difficult to analyze using the conventional tabular presentation of import or export data for one country.  For comparing the trade structure of countries, a matrix presentation of trade data is required.  These matrixes provide excellent information on the supplying and consuming countries of these raw materials and they also provide a useful tool to check the accuracy of the reported trade data by performing a back-trade comparison (partners data).  These tables also allow assessing the exports/imports of a country when no reported data is available by taking into consideration what its partners report as trade with that same country (back-trade).  The last trade matrixes were published in July 2009. 

<u>Annual Survey of Copper Mines and Plants (Item S7)</u> ICSG publishes bi-annually a Directory of Copper Mines and Plants, which is continuously updated with company reports and information.  In complement to these updates, once a year, the secretariat undertakes a special update of the Directory with the collaboration of its Member Countries and industry.  Through a specific survey for each individual country, members are requested to give ICSG an update on their copper industries in order to help the secretariat compile accurate and reliable data. For non-member countries the survey is sent to industry associations or directly to companies. Responses from the annual survey are then processed and inserted in the database.  The 2009 annual survey was sent in May to selected countries and results were included in the June 2009 Directory. 

<u>ICSG Statistical Yearbook (Item S8) The ICSG produces a Statistical Yearbook that includes</u> annual statistics on copper and copper products, their production, usage and trade by country, as well as stocks and exchange prices, providing a global view of supply and demand for the past 10 

2 

years.  The Yearbook serves as a useful tool for consultations and analysis on the longer term evolution of world copper production, usage, stocks and prices.  The 2009 yearbook was published in July 2009. The Yearbook represents a source of revenue for ICSG through its sales. 

<u>Country Production Profiles (Item S9)</u> Special attention is given to countries where no global data are available through any official source or where no monthly data are obtainable in a timely manner for the publication of the Bulletins. Research work and data collection is developed in order to build mine by mine and plant by plant country production profiles, focusing on actual data and expected production levels. These profiles allow us to better assess the total country production rates and to better identify the evolution scenarios. Production country profiles have been created, and are regularly updated, on a company by company basis, for countri

es such as Congo, Zambia, Russia, India, Indonesia, Mexico, South Africa, Philippines, Botswana and Brazil, among others. Once set up, these profiles are continuously updated to provide data to the Bulletin and to the forecast. 

<u>Alloy Foundry and Ingot Production Statistics (Item S10)</u> ICSG conducts an annual survey on alloy foundry and ingot production data that is sent to the member countries.  The results of the survey are complemented with additional data gathered from other sources for several countries. Though total alloy foundry and ingot production data consist of comparatively small quantities, they complement the data availability for the first use of copper.  The last Survey results, along with additional data gathered, were published in March 2009 and the next publication is scheduled for March 2010. 

<u>Update and Maintenance of ICSG Website (Item S11)  Each month the Bulletin, summary Bulletin</u> tables, detailed Excel tables and the press release are uploaded to the ICSG site directly from the secretariat PC’s. Other uploads, updates or modifications are also undertaken when necessary. The secretariat recently upgraded the ICSG internet site (project P8). 

<u>Calculation of ICSG member country contributions to ICSG Budget (Item S12)</u> Members’ contributions are calculated based on the mine production, refined usage and trade of each individual country. Each year the contributions are calculated for the next year’s Budget based on available copper statistics. 

<u>Customers/Member Governments Data Requests (Item S13) The secretariat is frequently asked</u> questions about the nature of its statistics, the structure of the copper industry, or other topics related to copper. It is also frequently requested to provide custom data sets and long time series sourced from ICSG databases. Requests are currently responded in a timely manner and, depending on the nature of the request and subscriber status, fees are assessed. On an average basis ICSG receives around 3 requests per week either by email or by phone. This clearly demonstrates the visibility acquired by ICSG. On the other hand, replying and preparing data for these numerous data requests requires a considerable amount of time. 

<u>Accuracy of Forecast Report (Item S14) A report on the accuracy of the Study Group forecasts is</u> prepared on an annual basis. These reports enable errors in the Group’s predictions to be identified and analysed with the aim of improving the accuracy of future forecasts.  They also provide an incentive to members and their industry advisers to do their best to compile accurate forecast for their own countries. ICSG started to prepare this Accuracy of Forecast Report in 2007 and the next report currently being prepared will be presented at the October 2009 meeting. 

<u>Other Activities since the April 2009 meeting</u> 

- Preparation of data, information, presentations for ICSG meetings 

- Preparation of data for the Annual Nonferrous Me

tals Statistical Meeting to be held in Austria in September

- Promotion of sales of ICSG publications and data

## **<u>Projects Activities</u>** 

The following projects have “ongoing” status: 

- <u>Statistical Database Expansion and Upgrade (P9). In order to have a global interface of</u> capacities and production data, the ICSG TM1 production database (which includes the data for production, usage, trade and stocks) was expanded to include data on capacity that was running in Access (data that feeds the Directory of copper mines and plants. The project implementation and migration of data took place between December 2008 and March 2009 and final operational refinements were undertaken with the publication of the June 2009 Directory. This was a time consuming exercise for the Chief Statistician but successfully achieved. 

- <u>Improvement of ICSG Historical Data (P16)</u> The ICSG secretariat is often contacted by member governments, metals associations, industry, analysts, banks, consultants and university students that seek historical copper data series. The ICSG database contains fairly complete data from 1990 onwards, but previous data are missing, lack consistency, or most of the time are only available on a world basis (not all individual country data are reported). In order to allow for historical analysis of trends, better understand the evolution of individual countries and improve the quality, coverage and extension of ICSG data it was proposed that the secretariat dedicate efforts to the gathering and collecting of historical data. Funds in the amount of 2,000 Euros could be allocated to this project in case the secretariat would need to purchase data from statistical offices or metals associations. This task is made more complicated by the need to identify the right data sources with relevant and consistent historical data series. This is also a very time consuming project which has been put on hold due to other priority projects. The secretariat will endeavour to dedicate more time during the remaining of the year to working on updating and completing the historical series. 

- <u>Establishment of on-line statistical database/New server purchase (P14) It was agreed that</u> the new members’ and subscribers’ area developed for the ICSG website would include an online statistical database. 40,000 Euros were assigned to this project.  12,000 Euros have been already expended in a new server and TM1 database expansion. T

he Chief Statistician started discussions with IBM/Cognos on the best way to provide part of the ICSG database on line. A development plan should be ready for discussions at the October 2009 meeting. - World Copper Factbook (P5). The Factbook provides a broad overview of all facets of copper, from production to usage, major uses, health, environment, recycling and sustainable development. An updated and improved version was published and distributed at the end of 2007 and a PDF version was posted in ICSG website. The 2009 edition of the Factbook is scheduled for publication in the 4th quarter of 2009. 4 The following projects have not yet been undertaken: - Copper Scrap Trade Flows (P4) This project aims at identifying the flow of copper scrap between countries, identifying inconsistencies in reported country data (the difference between reporters and partners data) and at finding possible explanations for the discrepancies (a detailed description of the project is attached). The first part was initiated in 2005 and the project was put on hold due to the lack of available staff. It was suggested that this project be integrated into the new Scrap Project. - Market Transparency – General (P2). Funds available; to be developed. - Data on Copper Usage (P6) This project is currently on hold (see document ICSG/EEC27/4 “Proposal on Copper End Use Data Agreement with ICA”.
